total_supply_at_construction.meaning: totalSupply value pre-set by the HypoVault constructor
total_supply_at_construction.checkpoint: after constructor, before first deposit fulfillment

underlying_assets_at_construction.meaning: underlying assets owned by the vault at construction
underlying_assets_at_construction.checkpoint: after constructor, before first deposit fulfillment

total_assets_before_first_fulfillment.meaning: totalAssets (computeNAV() == assetsDeposited) observed before the first fulfilment

supply_at_start_expected.meaning: report-required starting supply: zero shares until assets exist
supply_at_start_expected.checkpoint: vault start, before any assets exist

shares_burned_for_tiny_assets.meaning: a withdrawal burns a huge number of shares while releasing only tiny (or zero) assets

assumptions: totalSupply and totalAssets are observed at the checkpoints named in the symbol declarations.

unresolved.description: The intent states a qualitative requirement (zero supply until assets exist) but does not define the expected starting supply as a numeric quantity beyond 'zero'; the expected symbol is bound to zero per the intent wording.
Report does not specify the checkpoint at which totalAssets == 1 is observed relative to constructor versus first fulfillment.

limitations: Impact is potential; the Boolean outcome records the reported possibility, not an inevitable effect.
The 'huge numbers of shares for tiny (or zero) assets' magnitude is not numerically bounded in the report, so V is a grounded Boolean.

links.reported_relation: Constructor pre-sets totalSupply = 1 000 000 with zero assets and totalAssets evaluates to 1 at first fulfillment, so shares minted are inflated.
fulfillWithdrawals uses Math.mulDiv with the 1-wei denominator, inflating/devaluing shares and assets on withdrawal.
